title: Acids, Bases and the Periodic Table

standard_text: Acids, bases and neutral substances are identified with indicators such as litmus and red cabbage juice; the pH scale. Elements are made of one kind of atom and are arranged in the periodic table; metals, non-metals and semi-metals. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 7, Matter and Materials: Acids, bases and neutrals; introduction to the periodic table)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): acids, bases and neutrals, indicators, the pH scale, elements, symbols and the periodic table. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Acids turn blue litmus red; bases turn red litmus blue.

body_html:
How to think about it

Acids (vinegar, lemon juice) taste sour and turn blue litmus red. Bases (bicarbonate of soda, soap) feel slippery and turn red litmus blue. Neutral substances (pure water, salt solution) do not change litmus. On the pH scale, below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral and above 7 is basic.

An element is a pure substance made of only one kind of atom. Each element has a symbol (O for oxygen, Fe for iron). The periodic table arranges the elements: metals on the left, non-metals on the right and semi-metals along the staircase line.

Example

A solution turns blue litmus red. Is it acidic or basic?

Acids turn blue litmus red.

Answer: acidic

Example

What is the symbol for sodium?

From its Latin name natrium

Answer: Na

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all acids are dangerous.
  • Thinking pH 7 is acidic.
  • Mixing up element symbols such as Co and CO.
